problems.question: Seed and publish a curated OSS evidence set without confusing popularity or catalog presence with contextual fit.
Build a deterministic local Python research core without inventing command parsing, validation, safe querying, or canonical JSON.
Coordinate prior-art research locally without making a hosted backend or personal GitHub mutation the product core.
Run a reproducible quality gate for a typed Python CLI across environments, behavior, and hosted source analysis.
Publish searchable static technical documentation and review its prose without making an editorial model authoritative.

covers: Provides human-curated public seed data and transparent ecosystem discovery inputs.
watch: Its scores and inclusion choices are discovery provenance, not evidence of fit for a concrete problem.
reconsider_when: License, published data shape, or attribution terms change.

covers: Demonstrates a generator-backed catalog workflow and the maintenance concerns such a pipeline must own.
watch: GPL and content boundaries plus observed last-known-good failures make embedding it unjustified here.
reconsider_when: License documentation and fail-closed last-known-good behavior are resolved upstream.

covers: Shows how a lightweight static catalog can publish structured project information without a custom hosted application.
watch: Stable releases and an auditable deterministic export contract were not established in the reviewed evidence.
reconsider_when: A stable release and documented deterministic export contract exist.

covers: Evaluates safe local expressions over one documented candidate view without arbitrary Python execution.
watch: It is only the advanced filter evaluator; native gates and the exposed query view remain project-owned.
reconsider_when: A required real-world filter cannot be expressed safely.

covers: Owns mature command parsing and help generation while typed domain validation stays outside the parser.
watch: It does not define research semantics, evidence policy, or the command lifecycle.
reconsider_when: The selected major version becomes incompatible or an already-used component fully owns parsing.

covers: Validates strict versioned records and generates JSON Schema at the external data boundary.
watch: Workflow rules, canonical hashing, and state transitions must remain explicit outside model validation.
reconsider_when: A major version breaks the strict immutable record boundary.

covers: Supplies standards-based canonical JSON bytes so content identity does not rely on ordinary sorted JSON.
watch: It canonicalizes bytes only; immutable receipt policy and safe state persistence remain separate responsibilities.
reconsider_when: Published RFC vectors fail or compatibility changes.

covers: Provides useful prior art for searching and organizing an existing GitHub Stars collection.
watch: Credential storage, provider, plugin, and release-provenance boundaries keep it out of this runtime.
reconsider_when: Credential storage, outbound boundaries, and verifiable release provenance are independently resolved.

covers: Demonstrates a hosted interface for browsing and organizing starred repositories.
watch: Supabase, provider, telemetry, and direct mutation surfaces are disproportionate to a local evidence core.
reconsider_when: A local static boundary with no direct mutation or analytics becomes the default.

covers: Owns the residual problem, evidence, decision, and freshness relation while established tools keep their native roles.
watch: Discovery still requires an explicit research plan; it is not a general natural-language recommendation engine.
reconsider_when: An established component supplies the complete residual under the same privacy and mutation guarantees.

covers: Owns the reproducible Python environment, lock, execution, and build orchestration.
watch: It is the environment owner, not a replacement for tests, typing, linting, or hosted security analysis.
reconsider_when: The lock or cross-platform execution contract stops being reproducible.

covers: Supplies hosted repository-native source analysis and SARIF reporting in GitHub Actions.
watch: It is GitHub-hosted and does not replace dependency, workflow, typing, or behavior checks.
reconsider_when: GitHub changes the supported action or the selected SHA is no longer valid.

covers: Runs readable scenario and contract tests across supported Python versions.
watch: Property generation and branch visibility remain distinct Hypothesis and coverage.py roles.
reconsider_when: Supported Python compatibility or plugin behavior becomes unsuitable.

covers: Provides pinned selective-context and source-driven-development guidance for the editorial workflow.
watch: The skills are reviewed guidance only; they are neither runtime dependencies nor factual authorities.
reconsider_when: A later pinned revision is fully reviewed and materially improves the workflow.

covers: Supplies the pinned First Reader method used for context-free review of first-contact public surfaces.
watch: The parent repository is a learning map, not a production dependency or blanket endorsement.
unknowns: Simulated reader responses are hypotheses rather than measured user behavior.
reconsider_when: Reader reviews fail to find the primary path or require sending unpublished prose to a hosted service.

covers: Runs repeatable offline prose checks across hand-authored public Markdown.
watch: It can flag deterministic patterns but cannot establish factual truth, reader usefulness, or editorial judgment.
reconsider_when: The pinned version cannot lint selected sources deterministically or project rules create repeated false positives.

covers: Builds responsive Markdown pages, tags, and private client-side search without a custom frontend.
watch: The pinned pre-1.0 version remains removable and must keep proving deterministic, accessible, no-runtime-network output.
reconsider_when: Strict build, search, accessibility, or no-third-party-request validation fails.

briefs.title: Publish a curated OSS evidence set
what_appears_covered: Human-curated seed data can provide transparent discovery provenance.
Static generation can publish structured project information without a bespoke hosted UI.
what_remains_unresolved: Catalog presence and popularity still do not establish problem-specific fit.
A safe publisher still needs explicit source contracts and last-known-good failure behavior.

briefs.title: Build a deterministic Python research core
what_appears_covered: Mature libraries already own command parsing, strict records, safe local expressions, and canonical JSON bytes.
Each capability can stay behind a narrow deterministic adapter.
what_remains_unresolved: The product-specific research plan, evidence gates, state transitions, and human answer still need a local coordinator.

briefs.title: Keep prior-art coordination local-first
what_appears_covered: Existing products cover Stars browsing, organization, and hosted management interfaces.
A local receipt layer can preserve explicit research context, evidence, decisions, and freshness.
what_remains_unresolved: General natural-language discovery remains outside the deterministic core.
Personal GitHub organization must stay an optional sealed operator action, not a prerequisite for research.

briefs.title: Run a reproducible Python quality gate
what_appears_covered: Environment locking, behavior tests, and hosted source analysis already have mature owners.
Their boundaries can compose without inventing one universal quality tool.
what_remains_unresolved: The repository must still define its supported versions, typed postconditions, coverage target, and complete gate ordering.

briefs.title: Publish and review static technical documentation
what_appears_covered: Static rendering, private search, deterministic prose linting, and bounded review methods already exist.
Editorial aids can remain separate from factual source and approval authority.
what_remains_unresolved: Human review must still decide whether claims are true, concise, useful, and supported by repository evidence.
Simulated readers do not replace measured reader behavior.
